items.question: What condition is necessary for the success of mantra and yantra?
premises: Success of mantra and yantra arises at that time
Success does not arise otherwise
items.inference: The efficacy of mantra and yantra depends on the stated condition being fulfilled.
items.plain_english: Then the success of the mantra and the yantra comes about, and not otherwise.

rows.grounds: that which must be kept secret regarding the guru

items.question: What obligation governs the secrecy of matters concerning the guru?
premises: The guru's secret must be kept
It must never be spoken
items.inference: Matters concerning the guru are subject to strict and perpetual secrecy.
items.plain_english: The guru's secret must be kept and must never be spoken.

items.question: To whom may the secret teaching be properly given?
premises: The teaching may be given to one endowed with devotion
It should especially be given to one of noble birth
items.inference: Transmission is restricted to qualified recipients, especially the devoted and noble-born.
items.plain_english: It may be given to one endowed with devotion, and especially to one of noble birth.

items.question: How should the disciple receive the teaching that has been declared?
premises: The teaching has thus been told to the disciple
The disciple is urged to be attentive and ascertain it
items.inference: The disciple must receive the declared teaching with careful attention and firm understanding.
items.plain_english: Thus it has been told to you, son; being attentive, ascertain it firmly.

items.question: What form of the auspicious guru should the practitioner visualize in meditation?
premises: The practitioner should meditate on the guru
The guru is visualized as auspicious, with a pleased face and slender waist
items.inference: Meditation requires visualizing the guru in a specific auspicious and pleasing form.
uncertainties: chivāṃ may qualify the goddess or the guru's auspicious form; taken here as describing the visualized form
items.plain_english: One should meditate on the auspicious guru as having a pleased face and a slender waist.

items.question: What additional adornments characterize the visualized form of the guru?
premises: The form has hands adorned with red bracelets
The form is beautified with jeweled anklets
items.inference: The meditative image includes specific ornaments on the hands and feet.
items.plain_english: And as having hands adorned with red bracelets and beautified with jeweled anklets.

rows.grounds: body radiant with a face resembling an arrow and a drop

items.question: How is the radiance of the visualized guru's form further described?
premises: The form is illuminated by the face
The face resembles an arrow and a drop
items.inference: The guru's visualized body is defined by a distinctive radiant facial appearance.
uncertainties: śara+bindu+pratīkāśa is a technical visual comparison; exact iconographic referent uncertain
items.plain_english: Whose form is illuminated by a face resembling an arrow and a drop.

items.question: What ritual action should follow the prescribed meditation on the guru?
premises: The practitioner has meditated in the prescribed manner
Worship should be performed after that meditation
items.inference: Ritual worship is to be performed subsequent to the visualization.
items.plain_english: Having meditated thus, one should perform worship.

rows.grounds: bestower of dharma, artha, kama, moksha

items.question: What benefit is attributed to the deity invoked through this worship?
premises: The deity is declared at that stage of worship
The deity grants the fruits of the four aims of life
items.inference: The invoked deity bestows the complete range of human and spiritual goals.
items.plain_english: Then the deity, so named, is declared to be the giver of the fruits of the four aims of life.

items.question: Which divine powers are invoked to protect the eyes and the whole body?
premises: The seed syllable klīṃ is invoked to protect the two eyes
Sadāśiva is invoked to protect the practitioner's entire body
items.inference: Protection is assigned to specific mantra powers and deities for different parts of the body.
items.plain_english: May the seed syllable klīṃ protect my two eyes, and may Sadāśiva protect all my limbs.

items.question: Which mantra powers are assigned to protect the shoulders and arms?
premises: The seed syllable śrīṃ is invoked for the shoulder region
The mantra hasakhaphreṃ is invoked for the pair of arms
items.inference: Distinct mantra syllables are mapped to the protection of specific upper body parts.
items.plain_english: May the seed syllable śrīṃ protect my shoulder region, and may hasakhaphreṃ protect my pair of arms.

items.question: Which syllables are invoked to protect the region below and the heart?
premises: The letter kṣa is invoked to protect the region below that
The letter la is invoked to protect the heart
items.inference: Specific syllables are assigned protective functions for the lower region and the heart.
uncertainties: tad+adhaḥ refers to a region below a previously mentioned part; exact referent depends on prior context
items.plain_english: May the letter kṣa protect the region below that, and may the letter la protect my heart.

rows.grounds: the left side of the body

items.question: Which syllables are invoked to protect the left side and the spine?
premises: The syllable hūṃ is invoked to protect the left side
The letter sa is invoked to protect the spine
items.inference: Protective syllables are assigned to the left side of the body and the spinal column.
items.plain_english: May the syllable hūṃ protect the left side, and may the letter sa indeed protect the spine.

items.question: Which syllables are invoked to protect the finger and the nail?
premises: The letter ma is invoked to protect the finger
The letter la is invoked to protect the nail
items.inference: Distinct syllables are assigned to protect the finger and the nail.
uncertainties: guliṃ may refer to a finger or a specific digit; exact referent uncertain
items.plain_english: May the letter ma protect the finger, and may the letter la protect my nail.

items.question: Which syllables are invoked to protect the feet and all the limbs?
premises: The syllable yīṃ is invoked to protect the pair of feet
The syllable hsauḥ is invoked to protect all the limbs
items.inference: Protective syllables are assigned to the feet and to the body as a whole.
items.plain_english: May the syllable yīṃ protect the pair of feet, and may hsauḥ protect all the limbs.

items.question: Which seed syllables are invoked for protection in the east and south directions?
premises: The seed syllable aiṃ is invoked to protect in the east
The seed syllable hrīṃ is invoked to protect in the south
items.inference: Directional protection is established by assigning specific seed syllables to the east and south.
items.plain_english: May the seed syllable aiṃ protect me in the east, and may the seed syllable hrīṃ protect me in the south.

rows.grounds: syllable or formula beginning with veda reference

items.question: Which protective powers are invoked for the southeast and southwest directions?
premises: The syllable aiṃ is invoked to protect in the southeast corner
The power beginning with veda is invoked to protect in the southwest
items.inference: Specific mantra powers are assigned to guard the southeast and southwest directions.
uncertainties: veda+ādyā is an elliptical designation; the exact syllable or formula intended is uncertain
items.plain_english: May aiṃ protect in the southeast corner, and may the one beginning with veda protect in the southwest.

items.question: How is protection invoked for the upward and downward directions?
premises: Worship and homage are directed upward and downward
Protection is invoked to be constant in those directions
items.inference: The ritual extends protective invocation to the vertical directions above and below.
uncertainties: syntax is compressed; the subject of avatu is not explicitly stated
items.plain_english: I worship likewise above, and with homage below; may there always be protection.

items.question: What exalted status is attained by the practitioner who fulfills this practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes accomplished and a divine attendant
The practitioner is declared to be Śiva manifest without doubt
items.inference: Successful practice confers a status identified with accomplished beings and Śiva himself.
items.plain_english: He is accomplished, he is a divine attendant, he is also Śiva manifest; there is no doubt.

items.question: What result is promised to one who recites this at the three daily junctures?
premises: One who recites at the three junctures is addressed in the teaching
Such a reciter becomes accomplished without doubt
items.inference: Regular recitation at the three daily junctures guarantees spiritual accomplishment.
items.plain_english: O goddess, whoever recites this at the three junctures becomes accomplished; there is no doubt in this.

items.question: What effect does the mere sight of the accomplished practitioner have on disputants?
premises: The accomplished practitioner is seen by disputants
Disputants lose their luster merely by seeing him
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner's presence overwhelms opponents without verbal contest.
items.plain_english: By the mere sight of him, disputants lose their luster.

rows.grounds: in a formal gathering or debate

items.question: What success in assembly is assured to the accomplished practitioner?
premises: The practitioner obtains victory in the assembly
The practitioner becomes equal to the speaker without doubt
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner gains assured victory and exalted parity in formal assemblies.
uncertainties: mama+tulyo: the identity of the speaker claiming equality is context-dependent
items.plain_english: He obtains victory in the assembly and becomes equal to me; there is no doubt.

rows.grounds: ruler in the realm of accomplished beings

items.question: What ultimate spiritual attainment awaits the accomplished practitioner?
premises: The practitioner becomes lord of the world of siddhas
The practitioner attains the state of liberation
items.inference: The culmination of this practice is both sovereignty among siddhas and final liberation.
items.plain_english: He indeed becomes the lord of the world of the accomplished and attains the state of liberation.

items.question: What restriction governs the transmission and disclosure of this teaching?
premises: The teaching must not be given to just anyone
The teaching must never be revealed
items.inference: This teaching is subject to absolute restrictions on transmission and disclosure.
items.plain_english: It must not be given to just anyone, nor ever revealed.
